group_results.reason: The added depth-limit setting is commented out. The supplied direct build does not enable it, so this change does not alter the target's static configuration.
The source uses the default limit of 1024; arbitrary query text can exercise parsing below and beyond it.
The new depth state belongs to the parser constructed for each query and is reached by the target's constructor call.
Exceeding the depth limit produces a parse error, which the target handles as an XPath exception in its default exception mode.
A node-set filter expression with repeated predicates can reach the new increment and limit check through query text.
Successful filter parsing restores the saved depth; the target supplies filter expressions as query text.
A location step such as /foo with repeated predicates reaches the new step-predicate depth check.
Successful step-predicate parsing restores the saved depth; such steps are available in the target's query text.
Slash-separated steps in query text reach the new relative-location-path depth check.
Successful relative-location-path parsing restores the saved depth; the target can supply slash-separated paths.
Binary expressions supplied as query text reach the new operator depth check; excessive chains yield a handled parse failure.
Every query enters expression parsing with depth initialized to zero; nested expressions reach its check and successful parsing restores the previous depth.
A successfully parsed query reaches the new zero-depth assertion after expression parsing restores depth.

build.reason: The recipe directly compiles the XPath fuzz entry with pugixml.cpp, and the repository configuration leaves XPath enabled. This is a static build-compatibility assessment; no execution result is supplied.

input.reason: The input bytes become only a zero-terminated query string. The constructor supports a variable-set argument, but the target always uses its null default; therefore no input can provide the supported state needed to compile a variable reference.

lifecycle.reason: The query is scoped inside the entry's branch or try block. Its destructor releases the implementation, and the input buffer is deleted after normal completion or a handled XPath exception.

control_flow.reason: The constructor routes query text into the parser. Successful parsing reaches the new depth assertion; depth errors return parser failure and become XPath exceptions handled by the entry.

rejected.requirement: The XPath compilation target must be able to supply a live xpath_variable_set containing a referenced variable when compiling a query that uses the supported variable-reference syntax.
rejected.target_route: A finite query such as "$x", with a live variable set containing x set to true, is recognized as a variable reference and can compile through xpath_query(query, &variables). The old entry passes only xpath_query(text), selecting the null variable-set default.
rejected.failure_condition: For every fuzz input containing a variable reference, the parser sees a null variable-set pointer and returns "Unknown variable: variable set is not provided". Thus the target cannot reach successful compilation of supported variable references.
rejected.alternative_paths: The complete old entry has one query-construction call in each compile-time exception branch, both using only text. Query bytes cannot create or pass a variable-set object, and quoted or differently spelled text does not supply the required state.

assumptions: The supplied recipe and repository defaults govern configuration; no unsupplied compiler macro override or execution result is assumed.
